title: Redwood monthly all-hands - October 2026
summary: Monthly company all-hands: company metrics, product roadmap updates (Dedicated + Private), reliability incidents review, hiring and org updates, security/compliance status (SOC2 progress), and Q4 priorities. Ends with Q&A and next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Khatri: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know it's a hectic week, appreciate you carving out time. Quick housekeeping, recording is on, questions in chat and we'll take some live ones at the end.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: Quick numbers first — usage up 18% month-over-month, new signups from marketplace are trending, and Dedicated renewals closed slightly ahead of plan.
[00:35] Speaker 1: Can you say the ARR bump again?
[00:38] Jordan Lee: Yeah, ARR motion looks good, pipeline healthy, not gonna over promise but we're seeing consistent growth across mid-market.
[00:47] Priya Patel: On product, short summary: Dedicated GA improvements — autoscaling policies now support burst lanes which customers wanted; Private — we shipped VPC peering templates and an on-prem install helper that reduces setup time by about 40% in our internal tests.
[01:10] Mei Chen: From eng side, a big shout to the serving runtime team — kernel selector improvements dropped tail latency at 95th by ~12% on our internal benchmarks. There's still follow-up around fast kv cache invalidations, we saw some regressions on long-running sessions.
[01:34] Diego Ramos: Right, the KV cache thing, it's actually more of a GC interaction. We fixed the hotpath but a small repro remains. We'll post an internal note and patch next week.
[01:51] Samir Khatri: Thanks — prioritized. On reliability, we had two customer-impacting incidents last sprint. One was a misrouted canary that exposed quota limits and one was a storage network blip affecting metrics ingestion. Diego?
[02:08] Diego Ramos: The canary routing issue stemmed from a routing policy mismatch after a rollout; a human oversight in the policy file. We've added stricter gate checks and a validation job to prevent incompatible policy merges. For the metrics blip, we've improved retries and partial writes resilience.
[02:31] Speaker 2: There's a note in the chat about the canary — any users affected?
[02:35] Jordan Lee: A small subset of Dedicated customers saw elevated 429s for about 7 minutes. We sent out incident reports and credits where appropriate.
[02:45] Priya Patel: Product roadmap — Q4 priorities: 1) Expand routing policies (region/cost-aware routing), 2) Optimize: automated batching suggestions and quantization profiles in console, 3) Private: streamline on-prem packaging and KMS integrations.
[03:12] Priya Patel: Also working on structured output tools and evals integration so teams can track quality regressions. We know that's a big ask for platform teams.
[03:28] Samir Khatri: Security & compliance update — Aisha?
[03:31] Aisha Gomez: SOC2 readiness: the control mapping is 82% complete, external audit kickoff scheduled for 2026-11-15. SSO/SAML flows fully documented, audit logs retention plan drafted. We still need a couple more evidence owners for infra controls.
[03:50] Mei Chen: On encryption — we've rolled KMS integrations for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private we added HSM hooks but still finishing the rotation automation.
[04:05] Speaker 3: Is there any customer asking for FIPS or extra modules?
[04:08] Aisha Gomez: A handful of regulated prospects asked about FIPS 140-2 in the context of HSM. It's on the roadmap as a compliance add-on.
[04:18] Jordan Lee: Sales update — our enterprise playbook emphasizes benchmarking (latency/cost) and private deployment offering for regulated verticals. We added a new benchmark kit for customers to run against Dedicated vs Hosted.
[04:35] Priya Patel: Hey quick product note — the benchmark kit will soon include a canned prompt set and a perf spreadsheet. We'll share a link after the call.
[04:45] Speaker 1: There was a question earlier about competitors — any shifts?
[04:48] Samir Khatri: We see continued competition from the big API providers on price and single-model simplicity; Anthropic and OpenAI keep tightening latency but we differentiate on deployment flexibility and unit economics. Also seeing more bespoke infra teams building in-house.
[05:07] Priya Patel: Also mention of a similarity to inference infra vendors; we're focused on the developer experience and cost controls like batching and caching, that is key.
[05:19] Samir Khatri: Hiring & org — Aisha?
[05:22] Aisha Gomez: Headcount plan: we're adding 18 hires this quarter across support, infra, and security. Priorities: two senior infra engs, one manager for reliability, three sales in EMEA, and hiring more solutions engineers to support Dedicated deals. Slack thread with reqs will go live after this all-hands.
[05:41] Aisha Gomez: Also people ops reminder — open enrollment for benefits starts next week.
[05:48] Diego Ramos: Quick technical deep-dive snippet — kernel selection improvements are in canary. We still need to tune quantized kernels for longer context lengths; some micro-batching improvements rely on a slightly different scheduling approach.
[06:08] Priya Patel: Roadmap cadence change: we're moving to monthly product slices instead of quarterly big pushes, to ship more incremental UX improvements and make rollouts less risky.
[06:20] Speaker 4: Any impact to customers?
[06:22] Priya Patel: Fewer large visible changes, more frequent smaller changes with stronger canarying. We think customers prefer less disruption.
[06:33] Jordan Lee: Finance note — runway remains healthy after the recent Series C deployment; we are tracking to plan but will be conservative on spend in Q4.
[06:45] Samir Khatri: Quick reminder on sales comps — close the year strong but don't over-index on discounting. We closed three Dedicated renewals with modest discounting; the elasticity is there.
[06:58] Speaker 2: Questions in chat about private on-prem SLA?
[07:02] Priya Patel: For Private on-prem we offer an enterprise support package; SLAs depend on install type, for VPC we have a baseline SLA, for air-gapped on-prem it's negotiated per-customer. We'll standardize the template pricing.
[07:18] Samir Khatri: Alright let's move to lightning updates from teams — SE team, Jordan?
[07:23] Jordan Lee: Solutions Engs shipped new onboarding templates, shortened POC cycle time by ~20% in trials. Please ping se-templates channel for the new artifacts.
[07:34] Mei Chen: Reliability — we've reduced mean time to detection using new tracing hooks in the console. We'll expand retention for traces for paid tiers.
[07:45] Aisha Gomez: People update — offsite in December planning underway, please add dietary restrictions in the form.
[07:55] Speaker 5: Payroll question? (laughs)
[07:58] Aisha Gomez: Payroll is fine, we promise.
[08:02] Samir Khatri: Ok Q&A live — first question from Marcus (engineering) in Seattle: what's the timeline for structured output eval integration?
[08:12] Priya Patel: We plan a beta by end of November with integrations to evals, plus a small SDK to run local checks.
[08:20] Marcus: Will that support function/tool calling traces?
[08:23] Priya Patel: Yes, we'll capture tool-call sequences and align them with prompt sets.
[08:27] Speaker 1: A note — there are a few typos in the console doc gantt.
[08:30] Mei Chen: We'll do a doc sweep.
[08:33] Samir Khatri: Last block — leadership asks and decisions. 1) Approve incremental budget for benchmark infra ($120k) 2) Approve two senior hires 3) Move forward with SOC2 audit kickoff. Any objections?
[08:50] Speaker 6: No objections from finance.
[08:52] Samir Khatri: Great.
[08:55] Jordan Lee: Quick customer story — large financial prospect ran our benchmark and liked the dedicated routing fallback; they're now in procurement.
[09:04] Speaker 2: Any blockers on procurement side?
[09:06] Jordan Lee: Legal asked for updated DPA and we are lining up an SSO demo.
[09:12] Priya Patel: One more product ask from sales — add a cost-explainability view in console so customers can see token-by-token costing per route. We'll prototype it in November.
[09:27] Samir Khatri: Okay wrap up. Thanks everyone. We'll send the recording and slides. A few explicit next steps and owners in the last two slides.
[09:39] Jordan Lee: Thanks all.
next_steps: Share updated roadmap deck and benchmark kit link by 2026-10-20
SOC2 audit kickoff: ensure evidence owners assigned by 2026-10-25
Post patch for KV cache GC fix by 2026-10-25
Recruiting: open reqs live in Slack by 2026-10-22
